note: Every proportion here names where it came from. The first glaze is the one printed in the Wikibooks yeasted-doughnut recipe, in that recipe's own ratios, under CC BY-SA. The rest are this project's own and say so under the result. Sugar under each result is worked out from the quantities on screen, at 7.5 g of sugar in a tablespoon of powdered sugar, 12.6 g in granulated, 13 g in maple syrup and 17 g in honey, and drawn against the donuts USDA has weighed. A glaze you make yourself lands wherever you take it.

bases.name: Butter glaze
bases.region: the recipe as Wikibooks prints it
bases.says: Butter, powdered sugar, vanilla, hot water. Goes on hot and sets clear.

anchor.title: Cookbook:Doughnuts (Yeasted)
anchor.note: The recipe's own glaze quantities — ⅓ cup butter, 2 cups confectioner's sugar, 1½ tsp vanilla, 4 tbsp hot water — scaled here to the batch you pick.

method: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Stir in the sugar and vanilla until smooth.
Off the heat, stir in the hot water a tablespoon at a time until it is thin but not watery.
Drag each donut through face-down within a minute of the fryer, then set it on a screen.

bases.name: Plain water glaze
bases.region: every shop with a glaze table
bases.says: Two ingredients. The one a strip-mall counter runs by the bucket.

anchor.note: No free-to-use shop glaze recipe exists to build on. What is cited is what a glaze IS — a thin coating of powdered sugar and liquid, poured or brushed on. The ratio here is this project's own; a shop thins it as the morning warms up.

method: Whisk the sugar into the liquid until no lumps are left.
Keep it warm. It thickens as it cools and stiffens as the shop heats up.
Glaze hot, drain on a screen, and leave it alone until the shell sets.

bases.name: Maple icing
bases.region: the West Coast, on a bar
bases.says: Thicker than a glaze because it has to sit on top and stay there.

anchor.note: This project's own proportions. Maple flavour on a commercial bar is usually maple flavouring rather than syrup, which is a fact about the trade and not a recipe; syrup is used here because it is what a home kitchen has.

method: Beat everything smooth while the butter is still warm.
Dip the top face of the bar only, and lift straight up.
Set it down icing-up. It firms in about ten minutes.

bases.name: Chocolate icing
bases.region: the front row of the case
bases.says: Cocoa, sugar, fat, hot water. Dark enough to read from the street.
method: Sift the cocoa with the sugar or it will stay lumpy.
Stir in the butter, then the water, until it pours off the spoon in a ribbon.
Dip face-down, lift, and go straight into the sprinkles if you want them to stick.

bases.name: Cinnamon sugar
bases.says: Not a glaze at all: a bowl of sugar and a hot donut.

anchor.note: This project's own proportions. The cited part is the practice — cider donuts are coated in granulated, powdered or cinnamon sugar while hot.

method: Mix the sugar and cinnamon in a deep bowl.
Drop the donut in while it is too hot to hold and turn it twice.
Eat it in the car park. This one does not keep.
